issues.legal_issue: The transitional legislature was competent to exercise the constitutional power of amendment.
material_facts: The constitutional amendment was passed by the provisional Parliament before both Houses of the regular Parliament had been constituted.
The constitutional provisions authorized the provisional Parliament to exercise all powers conferred on Parliament.
The amendment procedure referred separately to the Houses and the President, and the transitional provisions adapted that procedure for the provisional Parliament.
issues.conclusion: The provisional Parliament could exercise the power to amend the Constitution under the constitutional amendment procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 368 and 379, read with the constitutional scheme for Parliament in Article 79 and the provisions allowing certain constitutional changes by Parliament, show that the amendment power belongs to Parliament and that the provisional Parliament inherited Parliament’s powers. The different majority required for constitutional amendments is procedural and does not make the amending body a different institution. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_amendment_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a constitutional amendment passed during a transitional parliamentary period.
predicates.provisional_parliament_exercised_amendme: The provisional legislature passed the constitutional amendment.
predicates.transitional_body_received_all_parliamen: The constitutional arrangements assigned the provisional legislature all powers conferred on Parliament.

issues.definition: When a constitutional amendment is challenged and the provisional legislature passed it after receiving all parliamentary powers, the provisional legislature was competent to amend the Constitution.

issues.legal_issue: The President could adapt the constitutional amendment procedure to address difficulties arising from the provisional Parliament’s single-chamber structure.
material_facts: The provisional Parliament consisted of a single chamber while the constitutional amendment procedure referred to two Houses.
The President adapted the procedure so that it could operate for the provisional Parliament.
The adaptation left the special majority requirement unchanged.
issues.conclusion: The adaptation of the constitutional amendment procedure was within the President’s power and was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 392 authorized adaptations, including modifications or omissions, to remove any difficulties in applying the Constitution during the transitional period. Read with Article 379, this permitted adaptation before the occasion for exercising the relevant power actually arose. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: constitutional_amendment_challenge and transitional_parliament_had_one_chamber and presidential_adaptation_addressed_application_difficulty and special_majority_requirement_remained

predicates.constitutional_amendment_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of an adaptation affecting the constitutional amendment process.
predicates.transitional_parliament_had_one_chamber: The transitional legislature operated as a single chamber while the constitutional procedure contemplated two chambers.
predicates.presidential_adaptation_addressed_applic: The President modified constitutional language to make it workable for the transitional legislature.
predicates.special_majority_requirement_remained: The adaptation left the prescribed special majority requirement in place.

issues.definition: When a challenged adaptation addressed the mismatch between a single-chamber transitional legislature and a procedure framed for two chambers, while preserving the special majority requirement, the adaptation was valid.

issues.legal_issue: A constitutional amendment bill may be amended during its passage when the applicable parliamentary procedure permits amendments consistently with the constitutional requirements.
material_facts: The constitutional amendment bill was amended in several respects while passing through the legislature.
The constitutional amendment provision did not specify all details of the bill’s passage.
The legislature had rules for regulating its procedure and conduct of business.
issues.conclusion: The amendments made to the bill during its passage did not invalidate the resulting constitutional amendment.
issues.legal_principle: Article 368 prescribes the essential requirements for constitutional amendment but is not a complete procedural code. Articles 107, 108 and 118 inform the use of ordinary parliamentary procedure, including applicable House rules, so far as consistent with Article 368. The Court relied by analogy on Local Government Board v. Arlidge, [1915] A.C. 120, in accepting that a body entrusted with a function may use its own normal procedure unless the governing law says otherwise.

rule.if: constitutional_amendment_challenge and amendment_bill_was_changed_during_passage and amendment_procedure_left_procedural_gaps and parliamentary_rules_applied_consistently_with_constitutional_requirements

predicates.constitutional_amendment_challenge: A proceeding challenges the validity of a constitutional amendment on the basis of how its bill was passed.
predicates.amendment_bill_was_changed_during_passag: The legislature changed the constitutional amendment bill while it was being considered.
predicates.amendment_procedure_left_procedural_gaps: The prescribed constitutional amendment procedure did not specify every procedural detail for passing the bill.
predicates.parliamentary_rules_applied_consistently: The legislature used its procedural rules without conflicting with the express constitutional requirements.

issues.definition: When a constitutional amendment bill was changed during passage, the governing procedure left procedural gaps, and parliamentary rules filled them consistently with constitutional requirements, those changes did not invalidate the amendment.

issues.legal_issue: The prohibition on laws abridging fundamental rights does not apply to amendments made through the constitutional constituent power.
material_facts: The amendment inserted provisions that protected certain land-related laws from challenges based on fundamental rights.
The petitioners argued that the amendment abridged rights guaranteed by the Constitution.
The constitutional amendment provision authorized Parliament to amend the Constitution without an express exception for fundamental-rights provisions.
issues.conclusion: The prohibition on laws abridging fundamental rights did not invalidate the constitutional amendment.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 12, 13(2) and 368 must be read harmoniously. In Article 13(2), “law” means rules or regulations made through ordinary legislative power, not constitutional amendments made through constituent power. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_amendment_challenge: A proceeding challenges a constitutional amendment as inconsistent with guaranteed fundamental rights.
predicates.amendment_was_made_through_constituent_p: The legislature acted under the constitutional process for amending the Constitution rather than its ordinary lawmaking power.
predicates.challenged_measure_was_a_constitutional_: The challenged measure changed the text or operation of the Constitution through the prescribed amendment process.

issues.definition: When a challenged measure is a constitutional amendment made through constituent power, the prohibition directed at ordinary laws abridging fundamental rights does not invalidate it.

issues.legal_issue: Constitutional provisions that exclude a class of cases from fundamental-rights review do not require ratification when they do not change the courts’ powers.
material_facts: The amendment inserted provisions protecting specified classes of laws from being held invalid on fundamental-rights grounds.
The amendment did not alter the text or scope of the courts’ powers to issue writs or entertain appeals.
The petitioners argued that the provisions affected the constitutional provisions governing the courts and therefore required ratification.
issues.conclusion: The inserted provisions did not require ratification on the ground that they changed the courts’ powers.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Article 368 required ratification for amendments making specified changes to the relevant provisions concerning the courts. Articles 31A and 31B, as considered by the Court, changed the substantive scope of fundamental-rights protection for certain cases but did not change the powers conferred by Articles 226, 132 or 136. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_amendment_challenge: A proceeding challenges whether a constitutional amendment required additional approval by regional legislatures.
predicates.amendment_excluded_a_class_of_cases_from: The amendment made a defined class of laws immune from invalidation on fundamental-rights grounds.
predicates.court_powers_were_not_changed: The amendment did not alter the courts’ authority to issue writs or hear appeals.

issues.definition: When an amendment excludes a class of cases from fundamental-rights review but leaves court powers unchanged, ratification is not required on the ground that the courts’ powers were changed.

issues.legal_issue: Parliament may amend the Constitution to protect laws concerning matters within regional legislative jurisdiction from invalidation under fundamental-rights provisions.
material_facts: The inserted constitutional provisions protected certain laws concerning land and land rights from challenges based on fundamental rights.
Land was a subject assigned to regional legislatures for ordinary lawmaking.
The challenged provisions were constitutional amendments enacted by Parliament.
issues.conclusion: The fact that the protected laws concerned a regional legislative subject did not make the constitutional amendments invalid; Parliament had power to enact them as constitutional amendments.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished ordinary legislation on a subject assigned to regional legislatures from constitutional amendments. Under Article 368, Parliament had constituent power to alter the Constitution’s operation, including protecting specified laws from the operation of fundamental-rights provisions. The subject matter of the laws being protected did not remove that power. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

predicates.constitutional_amendment_challenge: A proceeding challenges Parliament’s authority to enact a constitutional amendment.
predicates.parliament_used_constituent_power: Parliament acted through the constitutional amendment process rather than ordinary legislation.
predicates.amendment_protected_laws_on_a_regional_l: The constitutional amendment protected laws dealing with a subject assigned to regional legislatures for ordinary lawmaking.

issues.definition: When Parliament uses constituent power to protect laws concerning a regional legislative subject, the regional allocation of ordinary lawmaking power does not prevent Parliament from enacting that constitutional protection.
